answer: The submission is honest and well-structured, but it reads as a concept with a prototype rather than an investable plan. Key improvements, in priority order: (1) Quantify the market bottom-up. Replace vague phrases ('several thousand neurologists', 'meaningful business') with a defined funnel: number of target clinics, patients per clinic, realistic enrollment rate, price, and resulting revenue, plus a clear path from the stated ~$50K ARR to a venture-scale outcome. Note that 10 clinics and 200 patients at $15-25/month is only ~$36-60K ARR; show the math and the plan to scale beyond it. (2) Replace admitted unknowns with concrete answers or a plan. Reimbursement is the core of the business model, so name the candidate codes (e.g., RPM CPT codes) and the requirements (device definition, minimum days of data, clinician time) or say precisely who will confirm them and by when. Do the same for HIPAA, FDA classification (is this a medical device or clinical decision support software?), and consent/storage of patient video. (3) Build the evidence case. Describe the validation study design: sample size, comparator (MDS-UPDRS tremor items), metrics (correlation, agreement), timeline, and what result would count as success. Report any data from the pilot, such as number of patients, adherence rates, patient and clinician feedback, and whether the clinic intends to renew. One paying pilot is the strongest asset here and is underused. (4) Sharpen competition and differentiation. Name specific competitors and their pricing, and explain concretely why clinics would choose a less-validated video approach (low cost, no hardware, patient burden) and what accuracy threshold makes it clinically useful. Address technical risks: lighting, camera angle, tremor vs. dyskinesia, and caregiver-dependent recording. (5) Strengthen the team and governance section. Resolve the entity and founder equity split before applying for funds, and move the neurologist advisor from informal to named and committed. State who owns regulatory and compliance, and how the team will work full time on this after graduation. (6) Make the ask specific. Give a budget with amounts allocated to validation study, legal, website and pilot expansion, a timeline with measurable milestones (e.g., number of clinics, patients, validation results by month), and what happens when the money runs out. (7) Tighten the writing. Fix grammar and typos (effects vs. affects, alot), remove hedging language, add one clear traction metric near the top, and include a short unit-economics line covering video storage cost per patient per month against the price. Overall: lead with evidence (pilot results, validation plan), convert open questions into owned action items with dates, and show the numbers behind the market and revenue claims.
